title: A Systematic Docker Troubleshooting Method knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “A Systematic Docker Troubleshooting Method”?
options: Disable all health checks so the service always appears healthy.
Collect evidence from state, logs, inspection and a repeatable test before changing settings.
Run broad prune commands before inspecting the failure.
Change several unrelated settings at once and assume the last one fixed it.
questions.answer_key: Collect evidence from state, logs, inspection and a repeatable test before changing settings.
questions.explanation: Evidence-led troubleshooting is safer and produces a reproducible explanation of the cause and fix.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering a systematic docker troubleshooting method, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to a systematic docker troubleshooting method fails, which response is best?
options: Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For a systematic docker troubleshooting method, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
